id_and_class.summary: Colin Morrison proposes that the direct physical correlate of our experience is the wavefunction of a single rare particle confined in a tiny brain region, probably one neuron, which he calls ‘the cavity.’ Sensory signals, memory and emotion shape the amplitude of that wavefunction, and the particle's genuinely free choice of position, which is our choice, steers attention. Natural selection tuned this system until the wavefunction's pattern formed subjective images that mirror the stimuli on our sense organs.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as a Particle Choosing Its Position

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Our consciousness is the experience of one rare, probably compound particle in the cavity; the intensity of a quale is identified with the amplitude of that particle's wavefunction at a given position.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Interactionist: the particle's subjective choice of position registers as a position measurement at detectors lining the cavity, and that measurement shifts the brain's attention.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (qualia are inherent in the basic units of matter; evolution shaped which qualia brains use, and new consciousnesses can come into being in certain circumstances)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: The particle experiences all its possible positions as our sense of the body and surrounding space, and it centers its experience on one location by subjective choice rather than cognition.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Each type of quale (color, sound, pressure, pain) corresponds to a distinct way sensory signals alter the wavefunction amplitude. Visual, auditory and somatosensory systems each evolved their own way of varying it.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A rare compound particle, its wavefunction, a neuron-sized cavity lined with particle detectors (likely supported on microtubules), and experience as an intrinsic feature of every particle.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Mainly evolutionary and conceptual reasoning matched to introspective features of attention; the physical correlates of qualia type and valence are not yet identified.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A single particle in a weak solution inside the cavity, surrounded by detectors arranged so that adjacent detectors direct attention to adjacent points in space.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (qualia types and intensities, valence), attention, binding, agency and free choice, and the evolution of subjective images.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Position measurements of the particle at detectors trigger shifts of attention to matching locations; sensory intensity, memories and emotions raise or lower the wavefunction amplitude at those detectors in real time.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: After each measurement the brain raises the amplitude around the chosen position, producing an ‘attention spotlight’ that holds focus nearby while leaving a little randomness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Localized in a single small cavity, most likely within one neuron.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: The particle's choices add limited randomness to attention, which helped groups of our ancestors spot dangers and opportunities because individuals did not all attend to the same thing at once.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Qualia that contribute to the wavefunction amplitude at the same place and time are always felt as connected, and probably also instances of the same quale type, which Morrison offers as his solution to the binding problem.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Sensory, memory and emotion circuits encode their information as variations in wavefunction amplitude across detector positions that map onto locations in external space.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Selection first used particle measurements to choose among high-priority attention targets, then tuned the system so selection probability tracked the chance of a location being the best source of information. Selection also made adjacent detectors map to adjacent points in space, so the amplitude pattern came to mirror sensory stimuli.
core_claims_and_evidence: Adjusting the probability of the particle appearing at particular detectors is far easier for the brain than rewiring circuits.
Unpleasantness increases the chance the particle lands far from its last position, adding useful randomness when behavior causes damage; pleasantness reduces it.
A tendency to shift attention between similar qualia favored organisms in which the same stimulus frequency always produced the same quale.
Since every particle is likely conscious, each one's choice of position places a tiny subjective effect in the experience of all others.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and evolutionary argument informed by quantum physics.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The theory needs a rare particle that has not been identified, plus mechanisms that keep exactly one such particle in a neuron-sized cavity.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Qualia types and valence have subjective explanations but still lack identified physical correlates. Morrison also notes that the particle's subjective centering is hard to tell apart from the brain-driven attention shift that follows each measurement.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Morrison grounds the view in panexperientialism reminiscent of Whitehead, but combining a micropsychist ontology with the claim that we are a compound particle requires that new unified consciousnesses can arise, which he asserts rather than explains.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Every particle has some experience, but our kind of consciousness depends on an evolved cavity-and-detector system around one particle, and Morrison does not say whether artificial systems could build one.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Since the subject is a specific physical particle, it follows from the view that copying the brain's information would not carry that subject over.
